extracted.intended_audience: comedians, festival organisers, venue programmers and general readers interested in comedy/entertainment controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and factors relevant to judging whether a stand-up comedy show is acceptable to a venue/audience and when a venue might cancel or defend a show. Covers content offensiveness, audience safety, complaints, warnings, intent/context, and venue responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No content that attacks people's dignity (racism/sexism/homophobia/misogyny)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that was considered “extreme in its racism, sexism, homophobia and misogyny.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venue policy: “We will not associate with content which attacks people’s dignity,” and material judged to be extreme in these respects can be deemed “completely unacceptable” and lead to cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience safety and comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: A large number of people walked out of Jerry Sadowitz’s show as they felt uncomfortable and unsafe to remain in the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience members feeling unsafe or uncomfortable (e.g., walkouts) is treated as a serious signal; venues may act immediately if attendees report unsafe conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume and seriousness of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pleasance said they received an “unprecendented number of complaints” regarding the show’s material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High volume or unprecedented numbers of complaints can compel a venue to respond, investigate, and potentially cancel performances even if the show ran previously without incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue duty to respond and protect staff
rubrics_metrics.description: “We had a duty to respond. The subsequent abuse directed to our teams is also equally unacceptable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues consider not only audience concerns but also staff welfare; abusive reactions toward staff are themselves unacceptable and factor into decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content warnings and signage
rubrics_metrics.description: The show had a warning that it contained “strong language and themes some may find distressing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a warning about strong language/themes is a recognised practice to inform audiences, but a warning may not prevent venue action if the material is nonetheless judged unacceptable by audiences or the venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of artistic intent and full context
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz: “A lot of thought goes into my shows ... I am offended by those who, having never seen me before, HEAR words being shouted in the first five minutes before storming out without LISTENING to the material.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should consider performer intent, the broader context of lines within a set, and whether isolated moments are being judged without hearing the whole performance; artists argue for contextual interpretation of provocative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of shocking/explicit elements as comedic device
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz defended a part of his act where he exposes his penis on stage, writing: “…getting my dick out is for the purpose of the funny line which follows it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shock or explicit actions may be employed as part of a crafted comedic effect; performers claim these elements are artistic devices, but venues and audiences may find such actions unacceptable regardless of intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and niche vs mainstream fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz: “I have never ONCE courted a mainstream audience … The show is what it is, for those who enjoy it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows aimed at niche audiences with provocative material may be acceptable to some patrons but not suitable for all venues or mainstream festival programming; alignment between content and expected audience matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and remediation for affected ticket-holders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pleasance said refunds were issued to cover ticket costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performances are cancelled, venues typically issue refunds and may be expected to apologise to those who bought tickets and travelled; this is a procedural remedy following cancellations.
